record.context_brief: Perfect matchings of the n-cube modulo powers of 2
record.original_question: Let f(n) denote the number of 1-factors (perfect matchings) of the n-dimensional cube. The paper reports a simple proof of the parity statement that f(n) has the same parity as n, and then states that similar but more complex reasoning should allow one to compute the enumerating sequence modulo any power of 2. Determine, in a self-contained explicit form, the value of f(n) modulo 2^m for arbitrary m ≥ 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q_n$ denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph, whose vertex set is $\{0,1\}^n$ and whose edges connect pairs of vertices differing in exactly one coordinate. Let $f(n)$ be the number of 1-factors (perfect matchings) of $Q_n$. It is known that $f(n) \equiv n \pmod{2}$ for all $n \ge 1$. 

Determine, in an explicit closed form, the value of $f(n) \bmod 2^m$ for every integer $m \ge 1$ and every $n \ge 1$. That is, find an explicit description (e.g., a formula or finite-state recurrence in $n$) of the residue $f(n) \bmod 2^m$ as a function of $n$, for arbitrary $m$.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches reveal results on the parity of $f(n)$ (Lovász's argument) and lower bounds on the 2-adic valuation of the number of perfect matchings in certain graphs (e.g., channels for planar graphs), as well as exact enumeration of $f(n)$ for small $n$ (up to $n=7$). However, no source provides an explicit closed-form description of $f(n) \bmod 2^m$ for arbitrary $m \ge 1$. The status appears unresolved in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Enumerating Perfect Matchings in n-Cubes
status_evidence.snippet: Exact enumeration of perfect matchings in Q_n for n ≤ 7; no closed form for f(n) mod 2^m given.
status_evidence.claim: Only exact values for small n are known; modular formulas beyond parity not provided.

status_evidence.title: Channels, Billiards, and Perfect Matching 2-Divisibility
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses lower bounds on the 2-adic valuation of the number of perfect matchings via channels, extending Lovász's parity result.
status_evidence.claim: Work on 2-divisibility of matching counts exists but does not yield a closed form for f(n) mod 2^m of the n-cube.

status_evidence.title: A005271 - OEIS
status_evidence.snippet: OEIS entry for the number of perfect matchings of the n-cube; lists values but no general modular formula.
status_evidence.claim: No explicit formula modulo powers of 2 is recorded.
